props.label: Main
props.html:
Exterior cleaning for builders and developers in Melbourne

We work to your programme, not our diary

For a builder the cleaning is not the issue. The issue is whether a lot is ready on the date it has to be ready, whether a defect can be turned around before a settlement, and whether the invoice matches the scope. That is what this page is about. The work itself is on the service page.

  • Rates per lot, by dwelling type
  • Sequenced against your handover dates
  • Induction, insurance and SWMS before the first visit
Get A Quote 0400 638 010
  1. Home
  2. Commercial
  3. Builders and developers

What a builder is actually buying

Predictability. A rate you can put in a budget before the job starts, a contractor who turns up on the date rather than in the week, and a scope that does not overlap with your internal cleaner so nothing is paid for twice or assumed to be someone else's.

The work is set out under builders and handover cleaning, including exactly what is in and out of the exterior scope. This page covers the commercial side: how it is priced across volume, how it fits a programme, how defects are handled and what documentation comes with it.

Where we fit a programme

Where exterior cleaning fits in a build, and what each point is for

On a single dwelling you might use one of these. On an estate, usually three.

How exterior cleaning is normally sequenced into a residential build programme.
  What it is for Why that timing
After the wet trades Getting render, mortar and paint splatter off hard surfaces and glazing The residue is still soft. Later it cures and needs acid, with the risk that carries on green concrete
Film and sticker removal Protective film and labels off glazing and frames Before a summer bakes the adhesive on and taking it off risks the powder coat
Pre-landscaping Driveway, crossover and paths cleaned before the landscaper arrives So the hard surfaces are not cleaned twice
Three to five days before handover The presentation clean across the whole exterior Close enough that it presents, far enough out that a trade marking something is still fixable
Post-PCI defect call out An exterior item raised at inspection, usually glass or concrete Turned around as fast as the site allows, because it is holding a settlement

Swipe for the rest of the columns

Volume and rates

How it is priced across more than one lot

A rate per dwelling type

Single storey, double storey, townhouse, apartment ground floor. Set once, so the exterior clean goes into the build cost rather than appearing as a variable at the end.

Sequenced, not batched

Lots cleaned as they come up to handover rather than all at once, so nothing is cleaned three weeks early and dirtied again by the trades still coming back.

One account, one invoice

Whether it is three townhouses or thirty lots, one scope and one account. Progress claims per lot or monthly, whichever suits your system.

Rework inside the window

If a trade marks a surface we cleaned within a reasonable window before handover, we come back without a new quote. Trades come back and surfaces get marked, and pricing that as a fresh job helps nobody.

Documentation before the first attendance, not at the gate

Site induction, insurance certificates, SWMS and any permits your contract requires are arranged before we attend. Tell us what your sites need and in what format at quote stage. Height work on a multi storey build comes with its own method statement.

Questions

From construction managers

Do you quote per lot or per hour?

Per lot, by dwelling type. An hourly rate is useless to a builder trying to cost a stage, and it puts the risk of a difficult lot on you rather than on us.

The rate is set from a walk through of one or two typical dwellings and then applies across that type for the project.

How quickly can you turn around a defect?

As fast as the site allows, and defects are treated as a different queue from scheduled handover cleans. They are normally holding a settlement, which makes them the most time sensitive thing on our list.

Being an existing client with the induction already done is most of the speed.

Do you do the internal builders clean as well?

No, and we quote that way deliberately so the scopes do not overlap. Most builders already have an internal cleaner, and splitting it cleanly means nothing is double paid for and nothing falls between the two of us.

We are happy to sequence around whoever does the inside.

Can you work on a site with restricted access?

Yes. Gated estates, shared access, limited parking and staged handovers are all normal. What we need is to know about them before the day rather than on it.

For multi storey work, access and anchor points are confirmed as part of the method statement rather than being assessed on arrival.

What documentation do you provide?

Insurance certificates, SWMS for the work being done, and induction completion for each site. If your contract requires a specific format or a particular system, tell us and we will use it.

Will you look at a job that another contractor has left badly?

Yes, and we will tell you honestly what is recoverable. The common ones are etched glazing from deposit left too long, acid burn on a green slab, and pressure damage to render. The first and third are usually not recoverable by cleaning, and it is better to know that before a walkthrough than during one.
